s:
Consider the following pairs:
1. TRAI — Telecom Regulatory Authority of India Act, 1997
2. CCI — Competition Act, 2002
3. FSSAI — Food Safety and Standards Act, 2006
4. AERA — Airports Economic Regulatory Authority of India Act, 2008
Which of the pairs given above are correctly matched?
x: All four pairs are correctly matched with the respective parent Acts of the regulators.
tq: Start from the sure parent-Act pairs and eliminate codes that omit a correctly matched regulator.
sec: Regulator → parent Act and year of establishment

s: TRAI was established on:
x: The Telecom Regulatory Authority of India was set up on 20 February 1997 under the TRAI Act, 1997.
tq: Discriminate between the establishment dates of different sectoral regulators.
sec: Regulator → parent Act and year of establishment

s: Which one of the following is correctly matched?
x: CCI was set up on 14 October 2003. FSSAI was set up in 2008, CERC in 1998 and AERA in 2009.
tq: Use the establishment year and date to separate closely related regulators.
sec: Regulator → parent Act and year of establishment

s:
With reference to sectoral regulators, consider the following statements:
1. CERC was initially established under the Electricity Regulatory Commissions Act, 1998.
2. The Electricity Act, 2003 is the present principal statutory basis of CERC.
3. The Electricity Act, 2003 was notified on 10 June 2003.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
x: CERC originated under the Electricity Regulatory Commissions Act, 1998; it is now governed by the Electricity Act, 2003, which was notified on 10 June 2003.
tq: Test the transition from an earlier statute to the present statute and retain all three precise statements.
sec: Regulator → parent Act and year of establishment

s: The Petroleum and Natural Gas Regulatory Board was constituted in:
x: PNGRB was constituted in 2007 under the Petroleum and Natural Gas Regulatory Board Act, 2006.
tq: Distinguish the year of the parent Act from the year in which the Board was constituted.
sec: Regulator → parent Act and year of establishment

s: Which of the following statements regarding PNGRB is correct?
o: It functions under the Ministry of Power and regulates inter-State electricity transmission.
It functions under the Ministry of Corporate Affairs and regulates combinations.
It functions under the Ministry of Petroleum and Natural Gas and regulates City Gas Distribution networks.
It functions under the Ministry of Health and Family Welfare and regulates food packaging.
x: PNGRB works under the Ministry of Petroleum and Natural Gas and regulates City Gas Distribution networks and authorises Geographical Areas.
tq: Ask which ministry and sector belong together instead of relying on the regulator’s name alone.
sec: Regulator → parent Act and year of establishment

s:
Which of the following bodies are statutory bodies under the Ministry of Power?
1. Central Electricity Authority
2. Appellate Tribunal for Electricity
3. Central Electricity Regulatory Commission
Select the correct answer using the code given below.
x: CEA, APTEL and CERC are identified as statutory bodies under the Ministry of Power.
tq: Check the complete membership of the ministry-wise group rather than selecting only the best-known body.
sec: Regulator → parent Act and year of establishment

s: The Competition Act, 2002 commenced on:
x: The Competition Act, 2002 commenced on 31 March 2003, while CCI was set up later on 14 October 2003.
tq: Separate the commencement date of an Act from the establishment date of the body created under it.
sec: Competition Commission of India - statutory basis, predecessor, agreements, dominance, combinations, appellate forum

s: The Competition Act, 2002 replaced the:
o: Industries (Development and Regulation) Act, 1951 and CCI
Companies Act, 1956 and Company Law Board
x: The Competition Act, 2002 replaced the Monopolies and Restrictive Trade Practices Act, 1969 and its MRTP Commission.
tq: Match the replacing law with the predecessor law and institution.
sec: Competition Commission of India - statutory basis, predecessor, agreements, dominance, combinations, appellate forum

s: Under the current composition described for the Competition Commission of India, it consists of:
o: A Chairperson and two to six other members appointed by the Central Government
A Chairperson and exactly six members appointed by the Supreme Court
Only a Chairperson and one member appointed by the President
A Chairperson and two to six members appointed by the State Governments
x: The current composition is a Chairperson and two to six other members, all appointed by the Central Government.
tq: Check both the numerical range and the appointing authority; both are common sources of traps.
sec: Competition Commission of India - statutory basis, predecessor, agreements, dominance, combinations, appellate forum

s:
Which of the following practices fall within the area of anti-competitive agreements dealt with by the CCI?
1. Cartels
2. Bid-rigging
3. Agreements harmful to competition
Select the correct answer using the code given below.
x: CCI acts against cartels, bid-rigging and other agreements that harm competition.
tq: Treat the broad category as including each specifically listed form of anti-competitive conduct.
sec: Competition Commission of India - statutory basis, predecessor, agreements, dominance, combinations, appellate forum

s: The CCI’s action against a dominant firm’s conduct, such as the WhatsApp privacy policy matter, relates principally to:
o: Authorisation of geographical areas for gas distribution
x: Penalising or examining conduct by dominant firms, including the WhatsApp privacy policy matter, concerns abuse of dominant position.
tq: Identify the competition-law concept from a short factual situation.
sec: Competition Commission of India - statutory basis, predecessor, agreements, dominance, appellate forum

s:
With reference to combinations under competition law, consider the following statements:
1. CCI reviews mergers and acquisitions.
2. A ₹2,000 crore deal-value threshold is intended to address acquisitions of start-ups that may otherwise escape traditional scrutiny.
3. Combinations refer exclusively to cartel agreements.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
x: CCI reviews mergers and acquisitions, and the ₹2,000 crore deal-value threshold targets potential ‘killer acquisitions’ of start-ups. Combinations are not exclusively cartel agreements.
tq: Reject the extreme word ‘exclusively’ and retain the two statements describing merger scrutiny.
sec: Competition Commission of India - statutory basis, predecessor, agreements, dominance, combinations, appellate forum

s: From 26 May 2017, appeals against orders of the Competition Commission of India lie to the:
o: High Court directly in every case
x: NCLAT became the appellate forum for CCI matters from 26 May 2017. Earlier, appeals lay to COMPAT, and a further appeal lies to the Supreme Court.
tq: Use the date to distinguish the present appellate forum from its predecessor.
sec: Competition Commission of India - statutory basis, predecessor, agreements, dominance, combinations, appellate forum

s: Which of the following is NOT correctly matched?
o: FSSAI — Director General of Health Services as its administrative ministry
FSSAI — Ministry of Health and Family Welfare
FSSAI — Food Safety and Standards Act, 2006
x: FSSAI is administered by the Ministry of Health and Family Welfare and is not under the Director General of Health Services. Eat Right India was launched in 2018.
tq: Find the wrong authority by separating an administrative ministry from an individual health-services office.
sec: FSSAI - parent Act, laws replaced, ministry, packaging regulations, Eat Right India

s: The Food Safety and Standards Act, 2006 consolidated how many laws and orders?
x: The Food Safety and Standards Act, 2006 consolidated eight laws and orders relating to food safety.
tq: Test the exact count rather than the broader description of consolidation.
sec: FSSAI - parent Act, laws replaced, ministry, packaging regulations, Eat Right India

s: Which one of the following was among the laws or orders consolidated by the Food Safety and Standards Act, 2006?
x: The Prevention of Food Adulteration Act, 1954 was among the eight laws and orders consolidated by the Food Safety and Standards Act, 2006.
tq: Identify the food-sector predecessor law among statutes belonging to different regulatory fields.
sec: FSSAI - parent Act, laws replaced, ministry, packaging regulations, Eat Right India

s: The Fruit Products Order and the Meat Food Products Order, referred to in the context of food-law consolidation, were issued in:
x: The Fruit Products Order dates to 1955 and the Meat Food Products Order to 1973.
tq: Preserve the order of two similar food-law instruments and distinguish their years.
sec: FSSAI - parent Act, laws replaced, ministry, packaging regulations, Eat Right India

s:
From 1 July 2019, food businesses are prohibited from using which of the following for wrapping food?
1. Recycled plastics
2. Newspaper
3. Glass containers
Select the correct answer using the code given below.
x: From 1 July 2019, recycled plastics and newspaper may not be used to wrap food. Glass containers are not included in this prohibition.
tq: Separate the two prohibited materials from a plausible but unlisted packaging material.
sec: FSSAI - parent Act, laws replaced, ministry, packaging regulations, Eat Right India

s: Eat Right India is best described as:
o: A Ministry of Power scheme for consumer protection, launched in 2019
A movement of FSSAI for safe, healthy and sustainable food, launched in 2018
A TRAI application for rating call quality, launched in 2018
A CCI programme for regulating food-sector mergers, launched in 2007
x: Eat Right India is FSSAI’s movement for safe, healthy and sustainable food and was launched in 2018.
tq: Match the initiative with its organisation, objective and launch year.
sec: FSSAI - parent Act, laws replaced, ministry, packaging regulations, Eat Right India

s: Under the 2026 FSSAI licensing reforms, registration covers food businesses with turnover up to:
x: Registration now covers turnover up to ₹1.5 crore; the earlier limit was ₹12 lakh.
tq: Distinguish the revised threshold from the earlier threshold and from licence thresholds.
sec: FSSAI - parent Act, laws replaced, ministry, packaging regulations, Eat Right India

s: Which of the following correctly describes the revised FSSAI licence thresholds?
o: State licence: up to ₹1.5 crore; Central licence: ₹1.5–50 crore
State licence: above ₹50 crore; Central licence: ₹1.5–50 crore
State licence: ₹12 lakh–₹1.5 crore; Central licence: up to ₹12 lakh
State licence: ₹1.5–50 crore; Central licence: above ₹50 crore
x: Under the revised framework, a State licence covers turnover from ₹1.5 crore to ₹50 crore, while a Central licence covers turnover above ₹50 crore.
tq: Read the ranges as a continuous sequence and reject reversed or overlapping thresholds.
sec: FSSAI - parent Act, laws replaced, ministry, packaging regulations, Eat Right India

s: Which of the following correctly distinguishes TRAI from TDSAT?
o: TRAI hears appeals under the DPDP Act, while TDSAT regulates food safety.
TRAI adjudicates disputes, while TDSAT fixes tariffs and quality standards.
TRAI regulates tariffs, interconnection and quality of service, while TDSAT hears disputes and appeals.
Both TRAI and TDSAT perform only adjudicatory functions.
x: TRAI performs regulatory functions relating to tariffs, interconnection and quality of service. TDSAT handles disputes and appeals.
tq: Separate regulatory and adjudicatory roles instead of treating both bodies as interchangeable.
sec: TRAI and TDSAT - separation of regulatory and adjudicatory roles

s: TDSAT was created by the:
x: Disputes and appeals were moved to TDSAT, which was created by the TRAI (Amendment) Act, 2000 and set up in May 2000.
tq: Identify the exact amending statute rather than a similarly related parent Act.
sec: TRAI and TDSAT - separation of regulatory and adjudicatory roles

s:
Consider the following statements about TDSAT:
1. It was set up in May 2000.
2. It hears appeals under the Information Technology Act, 2000.
3. It hears appeals under the Digital Personal Data Protection Act.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
x: TDSAT was set up in May 2000 and also hears appeals under the IT Act, 2000 and the DPDP Act.
tq: Check whether the tribunal’s jurisdiction extends beyond the telecom sector to the two specified digital laws.
sec: TRAI and TDSAT - separation of regulatory and adjudicatory roles

s: The chairperson of TRAI is:
x: Anil Kumar Lahoti is the chairperson of TRAI.
tq: Use precise office-holder recall for a statutory regulator.
sec: TRAI and TDSAT - separation of regulatory and adjudicatory roles

s: Which of the following statements regarding the TV Ratings Policy, 2026 is correct?
o: It abolishes regulation of TV rating agencies.
It transfers regulation of TV rating agencies to CCI.
It makes the Ministry of Information and Broadcasting the only regulator of TV rating agencies.
It makes TRAI the only regulator of TV rating agencies.
x: The TV Ratings Policy, 2026 makes the Ministry of Information and Broadcasting the only regulator of TV rating agencies, ending the overlap with TRAI.
tq: Identify the authority that receives exclusive regulatory responsibility after an overlap is removed.
sec: TRAI and TDSAT - separation of regulatory and adjudicatory roles

s: Which of the following is correctly matched?
o: APTEL — appeals against CERC and SERC orders
x: APTEL hears appeals against orders of CERC and SERCs. CERC deals with inter-State matters, while SERCs deal mainly with intra-State tariffs and consumer protection.
tq: Match each electricity body with its level of jurisdiction or appellate role.
sec: Electricity regulators - CERC, SERCs, APERC formation, APTEL

s:
With reference to electricity regulators, consider the following statements:
1. CERC deals with inter-State electricity matters.
2. SERCs deal with intra-State tariffs and consumer protection.
3. SERCs coordinate with CERC.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
x: CERC handles inter-State matters, while SERCs handle intra-State tariffs and consumer protection and coordinate with CERC.
tq: Compare inter-State and intra-State jurisdiction before selecting the complete combination.
sec: Electricity regulators - CERC, SERCs, APERC formation, APTEL

s: The regulator of carbon trading under the Carbon Credit Trading Scheme is:
o: CERC, while BEE administers the scheme
PNGRB, while CCI administers the scheme
SERCs, while APTEL administers the scheme
BEE, while CERC administers the scheme
x: CERC is the regulator of carbon trading under the Carbon Credit Trading Scheme, while the Bureau of Energy Efficiency administers the scheme.
tq: Separate the regulator from the body administering the scheme.
sec: Electricity regulators - CERC, SERCs, APERC formation, APTEL

s: APERC was constituted in 1999 under the:
x: The Andhra Pradesh Electricity Regulatory Commission was constituted in 1999 under the AP Electricity Reform Act, 1998.
tq: Distinguish the State reform law establishing APERC from later central and reorganisation laws.
sec: Electricity regulators - CERC, SERCs, APERC formation, APTEL

s: The AP Reorganisation Act, 2014 provided that APERC would continue as a joint regulator for:
x: The AP Reorganisation Act, 2014 retained APERC as a joint regulator for not more than six months, until separate SERCs were formed.
tq: Focus on the limiting phrase ‘not more than’ when interpreting a statutory transition period.
sec: Electricity regulators - CERC, SERCs, APERC formation, APTEL

s:
Arrange the following in chronological order:
A. Constitution of APERC
B. Establishment of CERC
C. Setting up of APTEL
D. Enactment of the AP Reorganisation Act
Select the correct answer using the code given below.
x: CERC was established in 1998, APERC was constituted in 1999, APTEL was set up in 2004 and the AP Reorganisation Act was enacted in 2014.
tq: Anchor the sequence with the earliest and latest dated events, then place the two middle events.
sec: Electricity regulators - CERC, SERCs, APERC formation, APTEL

s: APTEL was set up on 24 August 2004 under the:
x: The Appellate Tribunal for Electricity was set up on 24 August 2004 under the Electricity Act, 2003.
tq: Combine the exact date with the correct enabling legislation.
sec: Electricity regulators - CERC, SERCs, APERC formation, APTEL

s: The Data Protection Board of India has been created under which legislation?
x: The Data Protection Board of India was created under the Digital Personal Data Protection Act, 2023.
tq: Test the parent legislation of the statutory body.
sec: Data Protection Board of India - composition, powers, appellate forum

s:
Consider the following statements regarding the Data Protection Board of India:
1. It is an independent adjudicatory body.
2. It consists of four members.
3. It has an online complaints portal under the DPDP Rules, 2025.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
x: The Board is an independent adjudicatory body, has four members and provides an online complaints portal under the DPDP Rules, 2025.
tq: Check whether the institutional description, composition and digital facility all belong to the same body.
sec: Data Protection Board of India - composition, powers, appellate forum

s: The members of the Data Protection Board of India are appointed by the Central Government on the recommendation of:
o: The Chief Justice of India alone
x: Members of the Data Protection Board are appointed by the Central Government on the recommendation of a Selection Committee.
tq: Identify the appointing authority and the recommending body separately.
sec: Data Protection Board of India - composition, powers, appellate forum

s: Which one of the following is NOT a power of the Data Protection Board of India?
o: Awarding imprisonment for violation of the Act
Ordering urgent remedial action after a data breach
x: The Board can decide complaints and references, order urgent remedial action and impose penalties up to ₹250 crore. The Act does not provide for imprisonment.
tq: Find the option that reverses the stated civil penalty framework into a criminal imprisonment power.
sec: Data Protection Board of India - composition, powers, appellate forum

s: The maximum penalty that may be imposed by the Data Protection Board of India is:
x: The Data Protection Board may impose penalties up to ₹250 crore.
tq: Distinguish the exact statutory ceiling from nearby monetary figures.
sec: Data Protection Board of India - composition, powers, appellate forum

s: In exercising its powers, the Data Protection Board of India has the powers of a civil court under the:
x: The Board possesses civil-court powers under the Code of Civil Procedure, 1908.
tq: Apply the civil-court-power clue to the correct procedural statute.
sec: Data Protection Board of India - composition, powers, appellate forum

s: An appeal against an order of the Data Protection Board of India lies first to the:
o: National Company Law Appellate Tribunal within 90 days
Telecom Disputes Settlement and Appellate Tribunal within 60 days
x: An appeal from the Data Protection Board lies to the TDSAT within 60 days, and a further appeal lies to the Supreme Court.
tq: Separate the first appellate forum and limitation period from the final appellate forum.
sec: Data Protection Board of India - composition, powers, appellate forum

s:
Arrange the appellate route from an order of the Data Protection Board of India in the correct sequence:
A. Supreme Court
B. Data Protection Board of India
C. Telecom Disputes Settlement and Appellate Tribunal
x: The sequence is Data Protection Board of India, followed by TDSAT, and then the Supreme Court.
tq: Follow the institutional appellate hierarchy from the original forum to the final forum.
sec: Data Protection Board of India - composition, powers, appellate forum

s:
With reference to the Data Protection Board of India, consider the following statements:
1. A further appeal from TDSAT lies to the Supreme Court.
2. The first appeal lies directly to the Supreme Court.
3. The period for filing the first appeal is 60 days.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
x: A further appeal lies to the Supreme Court and the first appeal to TDSAT must be filed within 60 days. The first appeal does not lie directly to the Supreme Court.
tq: Use the appellate-stage distinction to reject the direct-Supreme-Court statement.
sec: Data Protection Board of India - composition, powers, appellate forum

s: In February 2026, the Delhi High Court issued notice on a plea alleging that the Data Protection Board and its appellate tribunal are:
x: The plea before the Delhi High Court alleged that the Board and its appellate tribunal are Executive-controlled.
tq: Recall the precise criticism raised in the contemporary judicial development.
sec: Data Protection Board of India - composition, powers, appellate forum

s:
Consider the following statements regarding appointment of chairpersons of regulators:
1. Appointment is made by the Central Government.
2. Appointment is usually based on the recommendation of a search-cum-selection committee.
3. In the case of the CCI, the committee is headed by the Chief Justice of India or the Chief Justice's nominee.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
x: Regulatory chairpersons are appointed by the Central Government, usually on committee recommendations. The CCI committee is headed by the CJI or the CJI's nominee.
tq: Verify the common appointment rule and the CCI-specific committee detail together.
sec: Regulators → chairperson appointment and removal

s: Which one of the following correctly describes the removal of a regulator's chairperson?
o: Removal by the Central Government on grounds listed in the parent Act and after a hearing
Removal automatically on completion of half the tenure
Removal by the Supreme Court only after a parliamentary resolution
Removal by the Central Government on any administrative ground without hearing
x: Removal is by the Central Government, but only on grounds specified in the parent Act and after the concerned person has been given a hearing.
tq: Ask who would perform the removal and whether statutory safeguards apply.
sec: Regulators → chairperson appointment and removal

s: Which of the following is NOT among the usual grounds for removal of the chairperson of a regulator?
o: Disagreement with a policy decision of the Central Government
Conviction for an offence involving moral turpitude
x: The usual grounds include insolvency, conviction for moral turpitude, incapacity and abuse of position. Mere disagreement with a government policy is not listed as a usual ground.
tq: Find the non-statutory ground among the recognised removal grounds.
sec: Regulators → chairperson appointment and removal

s: The present form of the proposed Higher Education Commission of India is the:
o: National Higher Education Regulatory Authority Bill
x: The proposal for the Higher Education Commission of India has taken the form of the Viksit Bharat Shiksha Adhishthan Bill, 2025.
tq: Distinguish the current name of a proposed institution from its earlier proposal title.
sec: Proposed regulators and bills - HECI and others

s:
Consider the following statements about the Viksit Bharat Shiksha Adhishthan Bill, 2025:
1. It was introduced in the Lok Sabha in December 2025.
2. It was referred to a Joint Committee of Parliament.
3. It seeks to repeal the UGC Act, 1956, the AICTE Act, 1987 and the NCTE Act, 1993.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
x: The Bill was introduced in the Lok Sabha in December 2025, referred to a Joint Committee of Parliament and proposes repeal of all three specified higher-education laws.
tq: Combine legislative date, parliamentary process and repeal provisions without confusing the three Acts.
sec: Proposed regulators and bills - HECI and others

s: Which of the following is NOT one of the three councils proposed under the Viksit Bharat Shiksha Adhishthan Bill, 2025?
x: The proposed Bill provides for Regulatory, Accreditation and Standards Councils. A Funding Council is not among the three councils listed.
tq: Use the complete three-member institutional list to identify the added distractor.
sec: Proposed regulators and bills - HECI and others

s: The proposed Digital Competition Bill seeks to pre-regulate:
o: Digital enterprises registered outside India alone
All online platforms irrespective of their size
x: The proposed Digital Competition Bill would pre-regulate Systemically Significant Digital Enterprises.
tq: Recall the exact defined category rather than broadening it to all digital platforms.
sec: Proposed regulators and bills - HECI and others

s: Which one of the following organisations has set up a Digital Markets Division?
x: The Competition Commission of India has set up a Digital Markets Division.
tq: Match the specialised digital-market function with the correct regulator.
sec: Proposed regulators and bills - HECI and others

s: The Competition Commission of India imposed a penalty of ₹213.14 crore on Meta/WhatsApp for:
o: Non-payment of goods and services tax
Failure to obtain a telecom licence
x: The CCI fined Meta/WhatsApp ₹213.14 crore for abuse of dominance.
tq: Link the exact monetary figure with the regulatory finding rather than the sector of the company.
sec: Universal angles

s:
Consider the following statements regarding the Meta/WhatsApp competition case:
1. NCLAT upheld the finding of abuse of dominance.
2. The appeal is pending before a Bench of the Supreme Court headed by CJI Surya Kant.
3. The penalty imposed by the CCI was ₹213.14 crore.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
x: NCLAT upheld the abuse-of-dominance finding, the appeal is before a Supreme Court Bench headed by CJI Surya Kant, and the CCI penalty was ₹213.14 crore.
tq: Track the case through the regulator, appellate tribunal and Supreme Court while retaining the exact amount.
sec: Universal angles

s: The Petroleum and Natural Gas Regulatory Board approved how many Geographical Areas in Andhra Pradesh for City Gas Distribution?
x: The PNGRB approved 10 Geographical Areas in Andhra Pradesh for City Gas Distribution.
tq: Test the exact state-level regulatory count using nearby numerical distractors.
sec: Universal angles

s: The target for PNG connections in Andhra Pradesh under the City Gas Distribution expansion is:
x: The target is 83.61 lakh PNG connections by March 2032.
tq: Read the quantity and deadline together to avoid a partial-number or date trap.
sec: Universal angles

s: As on 31 May 2026, the number of PNG connections reported in Andhra Pradesh was:
x: The reported number of PNG connections as on 31 May 2026 was 2,98,111.
tq: Distinguish the exact Indian-number-format figure from digit-swapped alternatives.
sec: Universal angles

s: Which district in Andhra Pradesh had the highest number of PNG connections in the cited City Gas Distribution update?
x: East Godavari had the highest number of PNG connections in the cited update.
tq: Use the location comparison carefully rather than selecting a more prominent urban district.
sec: Universal angles

s: The Digital Personal Data Protection Act has been criticised for amending which provision of the Right to Information Act to widen the exemption relating to personal information?
x: The criticism concerns the amendment of Section 8(1)(j) of the Right to Information Act, widening the exemption for personal information.
tq: Discriminate among nearby RTI section numbers and identify the provision dealing with personal information.
sec: Universal angles
